{{recipe|Brownies, Oatmeal Stout}} | [[Cookbook:Dessert|Dessert]]

This recipe, created by Joe Stutler, was a national finalist in the 2006 Cooking With Beer Challenge. The malt and oats in the beer enhance the flavor of the chocolate in these delicious brownies. Not overly cake-ey, not overly fudge-ey, the texture is nicely balanced. They're also decadently chocolate, and surprisingly light (thanks to the eggs). Great with a fruity beer, such as a lambic (Framboise, yum!).

==Ingredients==
* 1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] all-purpose [[Cookbook:Flour|flour]]
* ¾ cup unsweetened [[Cookbook:Cocoa|cocoa powder]]
* ¼ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
* 6 tablespoons unsalted room temperature [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]], cut into cubes 
* 8 [[Cookbook:Ounce|ounces]] dark bittersweet [[Cookbook:Chocolate|chocolate]], [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]]
* ¾ cup white [[Cookbook:Chocolate Chips|chocolate chips]]
* 4 large [[Cookbook:Egg|eggs]], at room temperature 
* 1 ½ cup superfine or granulated [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]]
* 1 ¼ cups (10 ounces) oatmeal stout [[Cookbook:Beer|beer]] (room temperature) 
* 1 cup semi-sweet [[Cookbook:Chocolate Chips|chocolate chips]]

* 1 package (8 ounces) [[Cookbook:Cream Cheese|cream cheese]], softened 
* ⅓ cup superfine or granulated [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]] 
* ½ teaspoon [[Cookbook: Vanilla|vanilla extract]] 
* 1 large [[Cookbook:Egg|egg]]

==Procedure==
# Preheat the [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] to 375°F. Line a 9 x 13-[[Cookbook:Inch|inch]] [[Cookbook:Baking Pan|baking pan]] with nonstick [[Cookbook:Aluminium Foil|foil]] (or grease and flour, or parchment paper…your call).
# In a medium bowl, whisk together flour, cocoa powder, and salt until evenly combined. Set aside.
# Melt butter, bittersweet chocolate, and white chocolate chips in a [[Cookbook:Double Boiler|double-boiler]] over very low heat, stirring constantly until melted. Remove from heat.
# In a large mixing bowl, [[Cookbook:Beating|beat]] eggs and sugar on high speed until light and fluffy, about 3 minutes. Add melted chocolate mixture, beating until combined.
# Beat reserved flour mixture into melted chocolate mixture. [[Cookbook:Whisk|Whisk]] in stout beer. The batter will seem a bit thin. Pour into prepared baking pan. Drop semisweet chocolate chips evenly on top of batter (some will sink in).
# Beat cream cheese in medium bowl with electric mixer on medium speed until smooth. Gradually beat in sugar. Beat in vanilla and 1 egg just until blended.
# Pour cream cheese mixture over brownie batter in pan; cut through mixture with knife several times for marbled design.
# [[Cookbook:Baking|Bake]] for 25–35 minutes on center rack in the oven, until a [[Cookbook:Skewer|toothpick]] inserted in the center comes out almost clean.
# Let brownies cool, uncovered, to room temperature. [[Cookbook:Dusting|Dust]] with confectioners' sugar before serving if desired.

==Notes, tips, and variations==
* Makes 18 (2x3 inch) to 24 (2x2 inch) brownies. For finger-food/snack portions you could halve these dimensions to get 36–48 brownies.
* Plating suggestion: swirl a raspberry lambic reduction sauce (12 oz lambic reduced to half, 4–6 oz seedless raspberry purée, 2–4 oz turbinado sugar, ½–1 teaspoon [[Cookbook:Cornstarch|cornstarch]]) on the plate; garnish with [[Cookbook:Mint|mint]] leaves, [[Cookbook:Raspberry|raspberries]], and [[Cookbook:Lemon|lemon]] zest.
